headline: Impairment charge drives Rexford to a net loss
summary_short: Rexford Industrial's Q2 FY2026 revenue was roughly flat at $245.5M (-1.6% y/y), but a $624.8M non-cash impairment charge on properties identified for disposition drove the company to a net loss of $504.1M (-$2.26 diluted EPS), versus $116.3M of net income ($0.48/share) a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue was essentially flat at $245.5M (-1.6% y/y). The quarter was dominated by a $624.8M non-cash impairment on properties identified for disposition in an ongoing portfolio review, driving a $504.1M net loss (-$2.26 diluted EPS) versus $116.3M net income ($0.48/share) a year ago. Excluding the impairment, operations were stable: NOI -2.0% y/y, Same Property NOI -0.5% y/y on 90.0% occupancy. G&A fell 30.7% on lower post-transition equity compensation. Cash fell to $32.2M (-92.5% y/y) after $300.2M of year-to-date share buybacks; management targets $1.5-2.0B of dispositions for 2026, and long-term debt was roughly flat at $3.26B.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: results were dominated by a $624.8M impairment on properties identified for disposition amid a portfolio review; underlying same-property leasing, occupancy, and cost trends were comparatively stable.

Company-disclosed: a $624.8M impairment charge, primarily from shortened expected holding periods on properties identified for disposition, drove the swing to a net loss; no impairment was recognized a year earlier.

Company-disclosed: Same Property rental revenue fell 0.7% on lower effective rents on new/renewal leases and higher bad-debt reserves, partially offset by higher occupancy and newly stabilized repositioning space.

Derived-arithmetic: operating income stayed roughly flat since the filing classifies the impairment as a non-operating item below the operating-income line; the small y/y dip tracks revenue's modest decline.
Derived-arithmetic: gross profit tracked revenue's y/y decline, with property expenses up modestly on higher property tax and allocated overhead costs.

Derived-arithmetic: the swing to negative EBITDA is driven almost entirely by the $624.8M impairment flowing through this measure, which (unlike the company's own EBITDAre) does not exclude impairment losses.
Derived-arithmetic: EPS swung to a loss in lockstep with net income; a 2.0% q/q reduction in share count from buybacks was a minor offsetting tailwind.

Company-disclosed: cash fell as $300.2M of year-to-date share repurchases and $198.0M of dividends paid exceeded $247.95M of operating cash flow and $255.0M of disposition proceeds net of $111.1M of capex.

Company-disclosed: $279.0M of new borrowings modestly exceeded $272.1M of repayments over the six-month period per the cash flow statement; the filing gives no property-specific reason for the small net increase.

Derived-arithmetic: equity fell q/q primarily on the quarter's $504.1M net loss and $100.1M of share repurchases, partially offset by other comprehensive income; the impairment is the single largest driver.
Company-disclosed: share count fell as the Company repurchased $300.2M of common stock year-to-date under its repurchase program, replaced by a new $1.0B authorization on July 20, 2026.
